name: Nevada Cares Campus Emergency Shelter
operator: Washoe County Housing and Homeless Services (lead/owner); Volunteers of America Northern California & Northern Nevada (shelter operator per City of Reno page and VOA job postings; current 2026 contract term not confirmed)
population: All adults 18+ (primarily men; couples, women and people with pets in limited capacity). Unaccompanied minors referred elsewhere. Women referred to Our Place first, accepted at NCC if Our Place is full.
address: 1800 Threlkel St (newer county pages use 100 Cares Drive), Reno, NV 89512
intake: Walk-in, 24 hours, low-barrier; bed availability on Washoe County Shelter Census Dashboard; no cap on length of stay
capacity: 549 beds (down from 604 after private cubbies were added, c. 2023); news sources still say '600+'. 2news Oct 2026 reported only 10 of 549 beds open on Oct 8, 2026.
funding: Washoe County (general fund/ARPA for construction; campus cost ~$78M per May 2026 News Anyway); City of Reno/Sparks interlocal contributions historically
notes: County became lead entity Sept 1, 2021. Seniors reportedly 30-40% of guests (July 2026 op-ed). April 2026 internal investigation of former HHS head Dana Searcy (resigned 2025) found operational failures in county homeless services. Address conflict: 1800 Threlkel St vs 100 Cares Drive. Phone conflicts across county pages (329-4141, 325-8200, 325-8210).

name: Nevada Cares Campus Safe Camp
operator: Reno Initiative for Shelter and Equality (RISE) as of July 1, 2026 (replacing Karma Box Project); Washoe County owner
population: Adults experiencing homelessness unable to access indoor shelter
address: Nevada Cares Campus, 1800 Threlkel St / Cares Dr area, Reno, NV 89512
intake: Admission criteria on county Safe Camp page; referral/application through Cares Campus staff (details not verified)
notes: Supervised outdoor tents/pods. March 2026: county moved to end Karma Box coordination contract early; RISE won competitive bid for Safe Camp and Resource Center, takeover July 1 (2026). Karma Box controversies (employee arrests) reported by Our Town Reno.

name: Nevada Cares Campus Resource Center / Warming & Cooling Center
operator: RISE as of July 1, 2026 (per 2026 contract award); Washoe County
population: All adults; anyone without a bed at NCC or Our Place
intake: Walk-in; seating, not beds. Warming center 24/7 from ~Nov 1 through ~Apr 30/May 1; cooling center activated in extreme heat/poor air quality. Call 775-329-4141 to confirm activation.
notes: 2025-26 warming center opened Nov 1, 2025. Year-round day resource center. 2026-27 opening not confirmed in search results.

name: Washoe County Winter Overflow (Nevada Cares Campus & Our Place)
operator: Washoe County Housing and Homeless Services with shelter operators
population: Adults (NCC); women/families (Our Place)
address: Nevada Cares Campus (Reno) and Our Place, 605 S 21st St (Sparks)
intake: First-come, first-served walk-in when activated, on or about Dec 1 through early April
capacity: ~84 overflow beds/cots at NCC; 24-25 cots at Our Place (182 total Our Place capacity cited in winter, May 2026)
status: open (seasonal; 2026-27 activation expected ~Dec 1, 2026 but not confirmed)
notes: 2024-25 season: 15,868 overflow bed nights; phased closure began Apr 7, 2025.

name: Our Place (Women's Shelter & Family Shelter)
operator: Volunteers of America Northern California & Northern Nevada (operator per May 2026 CHAB report; director Penny Adams); Washoe County owner. RISE was earlier operator at opening (2020).
population: Single adult women, senior women, families with children; animal companions allowed. Immigration status not required. Families screened for DV history.
intake: Contact Our Place intake/diversion staff; open 24 hours for residents
capacity: 158 women and 38 families (182 with winter overflow) per May 2026 CHAB; county policy: up to 138 women, 38 families, 28 seniors
notes: Opened June 8, 2020. Hosted 6-space safe parking pilot Jan-May 2026 (see separate entry). April 2026 investigation noted Our Place residents lost internet for weeks due to unpaid county bills. Capacity figures conflict across sources.

name: Our Place Safe Parking Pilot
population: People living in vehicles (registered, insured, operable)
notes: Pilot launched Jan 2026, scheduled through May 15, 2026; 7 people used it per May 12, 2026 CHAB summary. Staff planned to continue; extension past May 2026 not confirmed.

name: Good Neighbors Warming Center
operator: Good Neighbors (mutual aid) with RISE and rotating downtown churches (Reno First United Methodist, Trinity Episcopal Cathedral, Lutheran Church of the Good Shepherd, others)
population: Women, families, single fathers with children
notes: Started Dec 2024. 2025-26 season ran Nov 11, 2025-Mar 17, 2026 with expanded schedule and case management. 2026-27 season not yet confirmed as of search.

name: Reno-Sparks Gospel Mission Women's Emergency Shelter
population: Women (and children per some listings)
address: 355 Record St, Reno, NV 89512 (admin: 2115 Timber Way)
intake: Sign up at the Mission (directory info, not verified 2025-26)
notes: Faith-based. Address and bed counts conflict across directories; most sources pre-2025. Mission also runs long-term recovery and transitional programs (not emergency).

name: Reno-Sparks Gospel Mission Men's Cold Weather Emergency Shelter
population: Men
notes: Only older/secondary sources; current operation not verified.

name: Eddy House (24-hour youth shelter & drop-in)
population: Youth/young adults 18-24
intake: Walk-in drop-in center; central intake/assessment for homeless youth in Northern Nevada
capacity: ~20 overnight beds + 5 emergency beds + community living program (2020); 36-unit transitional apartment building added (planned spring 2025)
funding: Private foundations, Home Means Nevada (state) for apartments, grants
notes: Listed in May 2026 NCJFCJ Reno youth resource guide (as of April 2026). Bed counts are from 2020.

name: Children's Cabinet Safe Place (runaway/homeless youth crisis shelter)
population: Youth 12-17 in crisis
intake: Call/text hotline or go to any Safe Place site (RTC buses, McDonald's, Washoe libraries, Eddy House, etc.); case manager responds
funding: HHS Runaway & Homeless Youth grant, private
notes: Also runs Center for Aspiring Youth transitional living (opened 2017). Shelter location not published.

name: Kids Kottage
operator: Washoe County Human Services Agency (Children's Services); contracted shelter services provider
population: Children infant-18 in child welfare custody (not walk-in)
notes: July 2025 county newsletter reported critical bed shortage and high census at Kids Kottage. Not a public homeless shelter.

name: Safe Embrace
population: DV, sexual assault and trafficking survivors of all genders, LGBTQIA2+, disabled, and minor children; pet friendly
funding: Federal VOCA/OVW-type grants (affected by Jan 2025 federal funding freeze), private
notes: 2022: judge ordered temporary cease-and-desist and license revocation from neighbor lawsuit; Special Use Permit outcome not found. Listed in Washoe County HSA DV resource guide.

name: Domestic Violence Resource Center (DVRC) Emergency Shelter
population: DV survivors (women, children; new facility adds men's area and pet kennels)
capacity: 25 beds currently (temporary site); new [location withheld] 100 beds/42 rooms
funding: $30.7M private philanthropy for new building; grants
status: open (temporary location; new facility under construction)
notes: Shelter relocated fall 2025 for construction; new ~40-41k sq ft shelter targeted summer/June 2027 (was early 2027).

name: Inter-Tribal Council of Nevada Family Violence Prevention Shelter
population: Native American women and children affected by DV, sexual assault, child abuse, stalking
intake: Through ITCN Family Violence Prevention Program
notes: New permanent shelter (former office building converted, work started 2024); previously used motels. Opening date not confirmed.

name: Reno Housing Authority HPP Motel Assistance
population: Washoe County households homeless or at risk, income <60% AMI, Washoe resident for past year
intake: Referral only from partner agency staff, who help complete the application
capacity: Up to 60 days per household; limited by funds
funding: Nevada Housing Division (Account for Affordable Housing/HPP) + RHA reserves
notes: 2026-2027 partner solicitation published Aug 2026.

name: Washoe County CrossRoads (Men's, Women's, Women & Children's)
operator: Washoe County Human Services Agency; RISE staff operator (contract Jul 1, 2025-Jun 30, 2027 proposed)
population: Men; women; women with children; with substance use disorders (sober, peer-led)
address: Multiple sites incl. River House/Serenity homes, 480 Galletti Way bldgs 14/15, Sparks
capacity: River & Serenity homes up to 36 women (reopened July 2026)
funding: Washoe County HSA; Grace Church donations
notes: Really transitional sober-living, not emergency shelter; included for completeness. River House reopening ribbon-cutting July 8, 2026. Board approval of RISE contract not confirmed.

name: Salvation Army Reno
population: Men (rehabilitation program requires sobriety); shelter assistance line
notes: No verified current emergency shelter beds in Reno; main residential program is men's rehab. Provided meals at Aug 2026 Hawk Fire Red Cross shelter.

name: Family Promise of Reno-Sparks (Northern Nevada)
population: Families with children
notes: Only a GreatNonprofits listing found ('transitional shelter'); no 2025-26 confirmation of operation.

name: Catholic Charities of Northern Nevada - St. Vincent's Residences / Battle Born Housing Plus
population: Low-income adults seeking sober supported living
address: Battle Born Recovery Residences, 395 Gould St, Reno, NV 89512
notes: Supportive/sober housing, NOT emergency shelter; included because requested. No emergency shelter beds found. St. Vincent's Dining Room serves 1,400+ meals/day.

name: American Red Cross Hawk Fire Evacuation Shelter
population: Anyone affected by disaster; pets allowed
address: Reno-Sparks Convention Center Hall 4, 4590 S Virginia St, Reno
notes: Temporary disaster shelter, Aug 2026 Hawk Fire. Likely closed; not an ongoing homeless shelter.
